key_insight: Simple propagation-based baselines—filtered features plus an MLP, then label smoothing—recover much of the performance of more complex relational deep learning models.
engineering_relevance: For relational databases modeled as temporal heterogeneous graphs, this suggests strong practical value in low-complexity pipelines before adopting heavier GNN or Transformer architectures.
method: Apply fixed low-pass feature propagation on the relational entity graph to denoise and mix neighborhood information.
Train an MLP on the propagated features for the main prediction task.
Refine predictions with Correct-and-Smooth using a task-specific meta-graph that propagates historical labels among target entities.
evidence_signal: On RelBench classification and regression tasks, neighborhood-filtered features usually beat target-entity-only features and capture a substantial share of heterogeneous GNN performance.
watch_item: Correct-and-Smooth depends on a separately constructed meta-graph, so label propagation is not plug-and-play when target-entity connections are not explicitly given.
paper_title: Revisiting Simple Baselines for Relational Deep Learning
